literal: Food, clothing, and the rest, to all living beings, are not different; the possession of a sense of shame is human beings' distinction.
translation: Food, clothing, and other basic needs are common to all living creatures; it is the possession of a sense of shame that is the unique distinction of human beings.
modern: உணவு, உடை மற்றும் பிற அடிப்படைத் தேவைகள் எல்லா உயிர்களுக்கும் பொதுவானவை; ஆனால், நாணம் (பழிக்கு அஞ்சும் தன்மை) கொண்டிருப்பதே மனிதர்களுக்குரிய சிறந்த தனித்தன்மையாகும்.
explanation: This couplet highlights what truly defines humanity. While biological needs like food, clothing, and other basic necessities (referred to as 'eccam') are shared by all living creatures, they do not make humans unique. The poet uses the word 'nan' to mean a moral sensitivity or a healthy sense of shame that shrinks from doing wrong. It is this possession of a moral conscience ('nanutaimai') that serves as the true distinction ('cirappu') of human beings ('mantar') over other forms of life.
